metrics_missing.description: When a platform does not expose a metric, the remaining ones are reweighted and `confidence` is lowered.

Momentum.description: A score is never returned alone.

classification.description: `trending` requires top-decile rank in the comparison group, at least 1.5x the creator's own baseline, and growth across consecutive snapshots. `breakout` requires top 2%, 3x baseline, and still accelerating.

n.description: How many comparable videos this was ranked against. A small `n` makes any percentile weak, which is why it is returned rather than hidden.

floors_met.description: Whether the evidence bar for this claim was actually cleared.

gated_by.description: Present when the classification was capped below what the score alone would suggest. **Do not describe a gated result as trending.**
gated_by.example: Capped at watchlist: 2 spaced observation(s) over 3h. "trending" requires at least 3 across 12h.

components.description: Component values, `null` where not computable. Percentiles are within the comparison group, never raw rates.

creatorBaselineLift.description: Multiple of the creator's own normal performance. 1.0 is exactly normal.

analysis.description: The video's own stored analysis, when a response includes one. Not a number this run computed. Absent (or null) means either no analysis is stored, or this endpoint does not attach one.

pilotEvidence.description: Returned by `POST /v1/search/videos` and `GET /v1/videos/{video_id}` (null when the row carries none). Not returned by trending.

Metrics.description: Absent values are `null`, never `0`. A metric that was never observed is a different fact from a metric observed at zero.

VideoAnalysis.description: The video's stored analysis: what it says, and what it shows. Null when no analysis is stored, which is not the same as an analysis that found nothing, and is reported as its own state rather than as empty fields.

hook.description: The opening line or opening image, verbatim.

kind.description: claim | complaint | request | question, as classified by the analysis pass. Null when the stored record carries none.

about.description: The entity the claim concerns, or null when general.

sentiment.description: Overall valence the creator expressed toward the main thing the video is about (positive | negative | mixed | neutral | not_determinable). Null when no analysis is stored.

entities.description: Every brand, product, person or organization the analysis found substantively discussed, with the creator's stance toward each read from this video alone.

stance_evidence.description: The quoted words, on-screen text, or described image the stance was read from.

onScreen.description: What the video shows. Null for a video analyzed before the on-screen record existed.

trend.description: The cluster-level verdict, reported separately from the ranking.

verdict.description: `emerging_trend` needs at least 5 accelerating videos from 3 independent creators. `confirmed_trend` needs 15 videos from 8 creators, top-5% cluster velocity, and no single creator holding more than 50% of the cluster's views. `cannot_tell` means no video in the cluster has an acceleration measurement, which takes three metric snapshots (most often a frozen archive with none), so acceleration could not be measured. It is not the same as `not_a_trend`, which means videos were measured and found flat: report `cannot_tell` as unknown, never as evidence the subject is not trending.

posts_trend_grade.description: How many posts have enough observation history to be classified beyond `watchlist`.

excluded_by_brand_profile.description: Results withheld by the brand profile's exclusion list.

excluded_by_judge.description: Results withheld because the corpus judge (the subject-collision check every collected row goes through) explicitly marked them off-subject. Never included in this count when it merely was not judged yet.

excluded_official.description: Results withheld because the author is a declared official account (`official_accounts` on the brand profile); this brand's own or a competitor's. Withheld for both: a subject's own post about itself is not someone else's voice.

caveat.description: A plain-language statement when the corpus cannot support the question asked: an empty corpus, no metric history, or too little history to classify anything. Pass it on verbatim.
caveat.example: No metric history exists yet for this workspace, so nothing can be scored for momentum.

brand_profile_version.description: Which profile version produced these results. Two runs against different versions are not comparable.

disclaimer.description: Ships on every response carrying view-derived numbers.
disclaimer.example: Views are observed content views (potential exposures), not ad impressions. Ad impressions require first-party or Ads Manager data.

adoption.description: How many distinct creators adopted this over time. A view count says how far a few videos travelled; adoption says whether anything spread. A creator is counted once, at their first post, so a prolific account is one adopter rather than a movement.

bucket_hours.description: Bucket width. Fixed per window so two analyses of the same window are comparable.

top_creator_share.description: Share of videos from the single busiest creator, 0-1. Travels with the series so a rising line cannot be quoted without it.

summary.description: One-line reading of the curve, safe to restate verbatim.

new_creators.description: Creators posting for the first time in this bucket: the adopters.

axes.description: Comparative bars for hooks, formats and topics. An axis is null when too little of the corpus could be classified.

medianViews.description: Median views for this bucket. The most common bucket is routinely the worst performing, so a count alone answers the wrong question.

unclassified.description: Videos this axis could not classify. Reported rather than hidden.

medianViews.description: Median views for this bucket. The most common bucket is routinely the worst performing, so a count alone answers the wrong question.

unclassified.description: Videos this axis could not classify. Reported rather than hidden.

medianViews.description: Median views for this bucket. The most common bucket is routinely the worst performing, so a count alone answers the wrong question.

unclassified.description: Videos this axis could not classify. Reported rather than hidden.

withheld.description: Axes not returned, each with the reason. Includes 'sounds', which no collected field supports.

actions.description: Next steps, with arguments pre-filled. Actions that are not implemented appear in `unavailable` with a reason: never offered, never silently omitted.

args.description: Pass straight through to the named tool.

reason.description: Why it cannot be offered. Shown so a gap is explained rather than discovered.

test_mode.description: Present only when the request used a `pk_test_` key: nothing was charged and no collection ran. A statement about billing, not about the data.

test_mode_notice.description: Present with `test_mode`. A sentence to show a person.

demo.description: Present only when this workspace is a Pepo demo workspace: the videos, creators and competitors are sample data, not the caller's brand. A property of the workspace, not of the key.

demo_notice.description: Present with `demo`. Pass it on so sample data is never read as the caller's own.

matched_on.description: `analysis`: the match was in the video's stored analysis (summary, hook, themes, claim text) rather than its caption or handle. `pilot_evidence`: the match was in reviewed pilot identity evidence (brand and product family).

excluded_by_judge.description: Results withheld because the corpus judge (the subject-collision check every collected row goes through) explicitly marked them off-subject. Never included in this count when it merely was not judged yet.

excluded_official.description: Results withheld because the author is a declared official account (`official_accounts` on the brand profile); this brand's own or a competitor's. Withheld for both: a subject's own post about itself is not someone else's voice.

excluded_paid.description: Matches left out as ads or sponsored. 0 with include_paid true.

search_method.description: **Read this.** States exactly which fields were searched, so an empty result is not mistaken for an absence of such video.
search_method.example: Token overlap over stored captions, creator handles, each video's stored analysis (summary, hook, themes, claims) when one has been run, and reviewed product-family identity when present. Versioned pilot rows require every query term to match, so a generic family word cannot substitute for a specific product noun. Raw transcripts, on-screen text, detected products/logos and audio are NOT searched because those fields are not present in this corpus yet, so an empty result is not evidence that no such video exists.

posted_from.description: Set when the search read a range of posting days, YYYY-MM-DD in UTC.

posted_to.description: Set when the search read a range of posting days, YYYY-MM-DD in UTC.

disclaimer.description: Ships on every response carrying view-derived numbers.
disclaimer.example: Views are observed content views (potential exposures), not ad impressions.

test_mode.description: Present only when the request used a `pk_test_` key: nothing was charged and no collection ran. A statement about billing, not about the data.

test_mode_notice.description: Present with `test_mode`. A sentence to show a person.

demo.description: Present only when this workspace is a Pepo demo workspace: the videos, creators and competitors are sample data, not the caller's brand. A property of the workspace, not of the key.

demo_notice.description: Present with `demo`. Pass it on so sample data is never read as the caller's own.

answer.description: The answer, one paragraph per cited video. Each paragraph ends on its own line with the citation: `@handle`, then an em dash (U+2014), then the video URL, then the best matching clip as `(m:ss` en dash (U+2013) `m:ss)`. A video with no known creator is cited as `(unknown creator)`. Null when `reason` is set.

reason.description: `no_index`: nothing indexed for this workspace yet (unbilled). `no_hits`: no indexed video matched within the window (billed one `corpus_question`). `unsupported_question`: the question asks for something no video could ever answer (audience demographics, sales or revenue, ad spend, or whether something is trending now, which is `POST /v1/trending`), decided before any search or read (unbilled). `needs_analysis`: none of the videos in the library (inside `window`, when one was given) is analyzed yet, so there is nothing to answer from (unbilled). When some are analyzed and some are waiting, the ask answers from the analyzed ones instead, and `library` plus `caveat` say how many were left out; `library` carries the counts and, when nothing is already running, `estimated_cost_usd`; call `POST /v1/library/analyze` to start it. `analysis_running`: the same gate, but a pass is already running for this brand; `library.analysis_in_progress` names it, check it with `GET /v1/collections/{collection_id}` and ask again once it finishes.

post_id.description: Usable with `GET /v1/videos/{video_id}` and `video_ids` when the video is in this library.

start_s.description: Best matching clip, seconds from the start of the video.

in_your_library.description: Present when `libraries` is `all`: false for a video only another library holds. Keep it with `POST /v1/library/add`; until then `GET /v1/videos/{video_id}` and `video_ids` cannot read it.

hits_considered.description: Videos actually read for the answer (at most `hits`).

index_videos.description: Videos in this workspace's index, one per duplicate cluster, so smaller than the library. Null for `unsupported_question`, `needs_analysis` and `analysis_running`, which are decided before the index is checked.

library.description: Present when reason is `needs_analysis` or `analysis_running`, and on an answer drawn from part of the library: some videos analyzed, some still waiting. `caveat` then says how many were left out.

indexes_searched.description: How many of this workspace's video indexes were searched. A large library is split across several indexes, and every one of them is searched.

indexes_unavailable.description: Indexes that could not be searched (deleted, or the provider errored). Non-null only when that happened. Their videos are missing from this answer, so read it as thinner than the corpus by that much rather than as a complete result.

degraded.description: Provider-thinned coverage among the cited hits. Present only when at least one hit fell back or went unanswered because the video provider returned HTTP 429, a live read or its asset lookup ran out of time (`provider_timeout`), the shared read-capacity wait expired, or a held read lease was lost.

asked.description: The request echoed back, so a null answer is actionable. `window` is the caller's own filter: `no_hits` with a window set means "nothing in that period", not "nothing in this corpus", and widening it is usually the fix.

video_ids.description: The videos the ask was scoped to, or null for the whole library.

cached.description: Present only when this answer came from the answer cache: produced earlier by `method` for the same video and the same question, with no provider call and no read billed this time.

retrieval.description: How this hit was found. `index`: a plain footage-index match (the default, so it is omitted rather than sent). `analysis`: the re-rank picked it from the stored analyses and the footage index did not surface it. `both`: the footage index matched it too.

used_on_screen.description: Present only on a `read_transcript` answer that relied on the video's stored on-screen record (a visual detail the transcript does not state), whether or not a transcript quote backs it too.

sources.description: How each cited video was answered: from its stored timed transcript and on-screen record by a text model (`read_transcript`, tried first), read live from the footage (`read_footage`, only when the stored text cannot answer), from the stored analysis (`stored_analysis`), or not at all (`unanswered`). `cached: true` means the answer was served from an earlier identical question about the same video with no provider call. Only an uncached `read_footage` source is billed, as one `video_read`. `degraded_reason` is present only when that hit was thinned by a provider 429, a provider timeout, a shared read-capacity timeout, or a lost shared read lease.

rerank.description: Whether the analysis re-rank ran before the footage index was searched: a text-model pass over the stored analyses (sentiment, hook, summary, themes, claims) that surfaces videos a footage search can miss, for example a "what are people complaining about" question landing on videos whose analysis carries a `complaint` claim. Null when the ask never reached the index.

picked.description: How many of the final hits came from the re-rank's own picks, before the answer was cut to `hits`.

skipped.description: Present only when the re-rank did not run to completion, in which case the answer is exactly what it would have been without this feature. Absent means it ran, even if it picked nothing worth moving to the front.

search_method.description: **Read this.** States what was searched. Only analyzed, indexed videos are read, one per duplicate cluster; captions are not searched here.

test_mode.description: Present only when the request used a `pk_test_` key: nothing was charged and no collection ran. A statement about billing, not about the data.

test_mode_notice.description: Present with `test_mode`. A sentence to show a person.

demo.description: Present only when this workspace is a Pepo demo workspace: the videos, creators and competitors are sample data, not the caller's brand. A property of the workspace, not of the key.

demo_notice.description: Present with `demo`. Pass it on so sample data is never read as the caller's own.

paid_withheld.description: Videos this ask found but left out as ads or sponsored, among the hits and candidates it considered. Present only when some were; `caveat` says so in words. Absent with include_paid true.

first_asked_at.description: Unix ms of the oldest question in this group within the window, or null when the group is empty.

last_asked_at.description: Unix ms of the newest question in this group within the window, or null when the group is empty.

questions.description: Newest first, capped at 50: enough to act on, not the whole window.

source.description: Which endpoint logged it: `ask_corpus` is `POST /v1/corpus/ask`, `search_videos` is `POST /v1/search/videos`.

result_count.description: `hits_considered` (ask) or `matched` (search) at the time this question was logged.

brand_own.description: True when the brand itself posted this video. A brand's own posts are never counted as signal by the workflow endpoints; null when unknown.

excluded.description: True when the subject check marked this video off-subject (or pilot evidence marked it ineligible). Excluded videos are withheld from every other read; this endpoint still returns one by id so it can be audited.

media.description: The playable file, when one was captured. `video_url_kind` says which of two different things `video_url` is: `stored` is a durable copy Pepo holds and can be played whenever, `cdn_signed` is the **signed platform url captured at ingest, which expires within hours**: treat that one as best-effort and fall back to `video.thumb_url` and `video.url`. Null on rows with neither, and on platforms that serve no direct file.

mime.description: Content type of the stored copy. Present only when `video_url_kind` is `stored`.

bytes.description: Size of the stored copy in bytes. Present only when `video_url_kind` is `stored`.

history.description: The observation series behind any momentum claim about this video: the evidence, not the conclusion.

unknown.description: Comments carrying no classification. Never folded into `neutral`: guessing would inflate the coverage number, which is the one figure meant to be trustworthy.

author.description: Handle, or the display name when no handle was captured.

author_handle.description: The handle alone. Null rather than the display name, so a client rendering `@` + this value never prints `@Jane Doe`.

evidence_note.description: States what grounding this video's analysis does and does not have.
evidence_note.example: Timestamped visual/spoken evidence is not stored for this video.

disclaimer.description: Ships on every response carrying view-derived numbers.
disclaimer.example: Views are observed content views (potential exposures), not ad impressions.

lens.description: This workspace's industry vocabulary: which words every tool and report uses for "product", "competitor", "SKU", "review" and "consumer". Inferred from `category` when omitted (music/label/artist/band/record → `music`, else `cpg`).

judge_category.description: What counts as on-topic vs. noise when the corpus judge reads collected posts for this brand. means.description: What on-topic content is for this brand, when judging collected posts.

other.description: What should be treated as noise, when judging collected posts.

exclusions.description: Topics this brand refuses to be associated with. Enforced server-side in every workflow: matching results are withheld and counted in `corpus.excluded_by_brand_profile`.

platform.description: Omit to match this handle on any platform.

owner.description: Must name an entry already in `brand_names` or `competitors` on this same profile, or it rides back in `official_account_gaps`.

official_accounts.description: This brand's and its competitors' own accounts. A post from one of these is withheld at read time from search, trending, share of voice, product and competitor results, as the subject talking, never as conversation about it, and counted in `excluded_official`.

official_account_gaps.description: One message per declared `official_accounts` entry whose `owner` matches neither `brand_names` nor `competitors`. Recomputed on every read, not just at write time.

estimated_cost_usd.description: What the refused call would have cost. Nothing was charged.

balance_usd.description: The workspace's actual balance, matching GET /v1/credits. Some of it may already be tied up in other active holds.

available_balance_usd.description: What is currently spendable after subtracting other active holds from the actual balance.

suggestions.description: Computed against your actual balance. The first entry is the largest version of your request that still fits.

field.description: Which parameter was malformed. Present whenever one parameter is at fault; absent when the whole body was (for example, not a JSON object).

view_share.description: Share of ATTRIBUTED views, not of the whole corpus.

summary.description: One line a client can restate. Leads with the refusal when the split is not quotable.

reliable.description: Deprecated: prefer `reliability`. True only when `reliability` is `"reliable"`. Previously also came back true for a corpus of unrecorded origin (`reliability: "directional"`), which is why it is being replaced: a client checking only this boolean quoted a directional split as solid.

reliability.description: **Check this before quoting any percentage.** `unreliable`: the corpus cannot support a share number at all: report `reliability_because` instead of the split, never a number. `directional`: how the corpus was gathered is not confirmed as category-level: a percentage may be quoted but only labelled directional/approximate. `reliable`: quote the split as-is.

reliability_because.description: The one reason behind `reliability`, restatable verbatim.

corpus_origin.description: How the corpus was gathered, derived from the collection runs behind it rather than supplied by the caller.

setup_gaps.description: Configuration problems (no brand names, no competitors) that prevent a share of voice. Distinct from a data problem: the fix is different.

comparisons.description: Videos naming both the brand and a competitor. Counted for neither side.

unattributed.description: Videos naming no brand at all.

window_hours.description: Hours the read covered; null when it covered all time (no `window`, or `all`).

excluded_official.description: Results withheld because the author is a declared official account (`official_accounts` on the brand profile); this brand's own or a competitor's. Withheld for both: a subject's own post about itself is not someone else's voice.

delta.description: after - before. Positive is a gain.

isRemainder.description: The synthetic row absorbing everything below the top-N cut. It is real and must not be dropped when summarising: it is what keeps a truncated breakdown summing to the whole.

reconciles.description: The rows sum exactly to `delta`. Computed, not assumed. If false the breakdown is defective and must not be presented.

analysis.description: This driver's own stored per-video read, when one is stored, not a number this run computed.

unavailable.description: Things this flow was asked for and cannot deliver, each with its reason. Declared rather than omitted, because a response that quietly returns two of three requested charts reads as 'there was nothing to show'.

postsInCorpus.description: Posts WE COLLECTED, never the creator's output. A low count can mean they post rarely or that we searched narrowly: the two are indistinguishable from here.

medianViews.description: Median, not average: one breakout against nine quiet posts gives an average that describes none of them.

bestViews.description: Reported alongside the median so a one-hit creator is visible as one.

evidence.description: How much this row is worth standing on. "provisional" means fewer than 4 posts: a median of two posts is just their average, and one breakout in the pair puts a creator at the top of the list on the thinnest evidence in it. Never present a provisional row as a top creator without saying so.

consistency.description: Spread around the creator's OWN median, 0..1, lower is steadier. Null when there are too few posts for it to mean anything, which is more useful than a number that does not.

safetyFlags.description: Exclusion terms this creator's captions matched. A hit worth reviewing: the absence of one is never a clearance.

analysis.description: This example post's own stored per-video read, when one is stored.

typicalViews.description: Median views over the posts that carry a view count, and only those. Null when none does (Instagram search never returns views). `medianViews` counts a post with no view count as zero and is kept for compatibility.

postsWithViews.description: Posts with a view count: the base of `typicalViews` and `breakouts`.

engagementRate.description: Median of (likes + comments + shares) / views over posts carrying views and an engagement count. Null rather than zero when none does.

breakouts.description: Posts at 2x or more of this creator's own typical views here. Measured against their own posts in this corpus, not their whole account.

followers.description: Stored follower count, as of when it was collected. Null is unknown, never zero.

followersSource.description: `creators_table` when this workspace's creators table holds a count; `post` when only the latest count stored on one of their own posts does.

region.description: ISO 3166 alpha 2, as a collector stored it. Null is unknown.

ranked.description: False when listed after the ranked creators (below `min_posts`, or no follower count under `views_per_follower`). Absent on the default order.

unknown_sku.description: True when the requested `sku` is not a configured product. An input error, not an empty result.

excluded_own.description: Posts withheld because they are the brand's own (`brandOwn`). A brand's own posts are never signal, and the brand is never a creator to send product to.

ranking.description: How `creators` is ordered. Ranked rows come first; the rest follow by median views.

below_post_floor.description: Listed after the ranked rows: fewer than `min_posts` posts here.

without_measure.description: Listed after the ranked rows: views per follower could not be computed (no stored follower count).

followers.description: Stored follower count; null is unknown. Absent when no audience join ran.

single_post_creators.description: Creators with exactly one post in the corpus. Present and countable but NOT ranked, and they must not be compared with the ranked list: one post has no median and no consistency.

safety_statement.description: Repeat this whenever you mention brand safety. A flag is a hit; zero flags is NOT a clearance: screening is keyword-based over captions only and cannot see video content or posts outside this corpus.

audience.description: What the follower range and regions did, counted over every creator considered (ranked and single post). A null count means that filter was not asked for, which is a different fact from zero. Null when the request stopped before any creator (an unknown `sku`).

in_range.description: Known follower count inside the range.

out_of_range.description: Known follower count outside the range: left out.

withheld_unknown_followers.description: No stored follower count: left out of the shortlist, counted here rather than dropped silently.

region_unknown_kept.description: No stored region: kept and marked unknown, because most collectors store none.

quality.description: Which creators lack which fields and what that costs: follower counts, regions and view counts.

notOwned.description: Everything the brand did not post: paid and earned TOGETHER. These cannot be separated: nothing in the corpus records whether a post was promoted, boosted, gifted or contracted.

ownedUnknown.description: True when no social accounts are connected, so even the owned share cannot be identified.

Collection.description: A collection run, as returned by every /v1/collections endpoint. `reason` is set when the run stopped for something other than reaching `target`: a cancel, a settle, or an error.

posted_from.description: First day of the fixed range of posting dates this covers, YYYY-MM-DD in UTC. Null for a window that ends now.

posted_to.description: Last day of the range, inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD in UTC. Null for a window that ends now.

collected.description: Videos landed in the library so far. This is what is billed.

coverage.description: Coverage of the collected set against the request. Shape varies by run.

cost_usd.description: Spend so far. Not final until `settled` is true.

settled.description: Whether billing has settled for what actually landed. False while the run is still going.

treatment.description: `full`: a corpus run follows collection. `collect_only`: rows only. A run recorded before treatments existed reads as `collect_only`.

corpus_run.description: The corpus run behind a full-treatment collection, once enqueued. Null before that and for `collect_only`. Omitted from `GET /v1/collections`, which does not look runs up.

finished_at.description: Unix ms, or null while still running.

monitor_id.description: Set when a scheduled collection (a `collection_topup` monitor) started this run.

scanned.description: Every provider item the run paged through, including duplicates and out-of-window drops. Not billed.

out_of_window.description: Of the videos scanned, how many were not kept because they were posted outside the window or range.

analyze_target.description: How many of the landed videos this run analyzes. The run looks for more candidates than this and picks the most relevant and most watched; null when it analyzes everything it lands.

chosen_for_analysis.description: How many landed videos were sent on to analysis. Null until the run has settled, or when it analyzes everything it lands.

kept_in_catalog.description: Landed videos kept in the library without being analyzed. They are free, searchable by caption, and `POST /v1/library/analyze` with `video_ids` analyzes any of them.

feed_yield.description: What each feed the run paged (a platform's keyword, phrasing, hashtag or creator account) returned, kept in the window, landed and dropped, so the breadth of a search can be read after the fact. Empty on runs that predate the record.

returned.description: Items the feed's pages held, including those the relevance check dropped.

in_window.description: Of the items that reached the window check, those inside it.

landed.description: New videos this feed put in the library.

dropped.description: Dropped by the relevance check: off subject or the brand's own account.

failed_platforms.description: Requested platforms that failed mid-run and were dropped while the other platforms carried on. Empty when every requested platform ran.

plan_id.description: Set when this run is one search of a collection plan (`POST /v1/collections` with `plan_id`).

given.description: Videos of target this search handed to the plan's other searches when it ran out of videos to find.

received.description: Videos of target this search took on from a plan search that ran out. Already included in `target`.

target_moved.description: Only on a run that is one search of a collection plan. A plan splits its target evenly across its searches; when one search runs out of videos, its unused share (and the credit held for it) moves to the searches still running, so the plan can still reach its total. The plan never spends more than was approved.

estimated_cost_usd.description: What this run is estimated to cost. Nothing was started or charged.

budget_usd.description: The `budget_usd` you sent. Absent when the workspace call cap, not the budget, fell short.

field.description: Present when `budget_usd` itself was below the estimate.

held_usd.description: Present when the workspace's default call cap, not `budget_usd`, is what fell short of the estimate.

CorpusRunStage.description: One stage of a corpus run, in pipeline order. `output` is the quantity billed at the stage's unit (judge → dataset_row_verified, enrich → content_enriched, analyze → video_analyzed, index → video_indexed, comments → comment_collected, sentiment → comment_judged; dedup is free).

label.description: Short plain-language name for this step, for showing to a person (e.g. `subject check`). Render this rather than mapping `name` yourself.

description.description: What this step is doing, as a sentence (e.g. `checking each video is really about this subject`).

note.description: Human line, e.g. "34 kept, 6 excluded as off-subject". Quality-gate warnings start with "warning".

CorpusRun.description: The staged pipeline a full-treatment collection hands its rows to. Settles once, at the end, with one billed line per stage that produced output; `charge_capped` means the stages metered more than the hold the collection left and the charge stopped at the hold. `warnings` are the quality gates that fired (too few rows kept by judge, too many collapsed by dedup). The run continues; the operator decides whether to cancel.

attempt.description: How many times a worker has claimed the run. A run whose worker goes quiet is re-queued; the third stale claim fails it.

current_stage_label.description: Plain-language name for `current_stage`, or null when no step is running.

cost_usd.description: Stage spend. Final once `settled` is true.

eta_minutes.description: Remaining stages × the measured per-stage time of this run; null until a stage has finished, and once the run is over.

Monitor.description: A saved workflow on a schedule with a hard monthly budget: the only thing in this API that spends money with no human present. Spend is tracked per rolling 30-day period; a run whose expected cost does not fit what remains is recorded as `skipped_budget`, and with `pause_at_cap` the monitor flips to `capped` until the period rolls or the cap is raised.

workflow.description: `trending` re-reads the stored corpus each run. `collection_topup` starts one `/v1/collections` run per subject in `params.subjects` each tick: the standing order that keeps a corpus current, and grows to more search terms over time via `POST /v1/monitors/{id}/update`.

params.description: For `collection_topup`: `{subjects, platforms, window, target, treatment}`, normalised: `subjects` is always an array here (1 or more entries), even when the schedule was created with a single `subject`. For `trending`: the `/v1/trending` body.

monthly_cap_usd.description: The hard ceiling per rolling 30-day period.

spent_this_period_usd.description: For `collection_topup` this includes the reservation of any run still in flight; it is corrected to the actual charge when the collection settles.

last_collection_id.description: `collection_topup` only: the collection the latest run started. Poll it on `GET /v1/collections/{collection_id}`.

MonitorRun.description: One execution of a monitor. Skipped runs are recorded too: a monitor that silently stops is indistinguishable from a broken one.

cost_usd.description: For `collection_topup`: the reservation while the collection is in flight (`summary.accounting: "reserved"`), the actual charge once it settled (`"settled"`).

collection_id.description: `collection_topup` only: the collection this run started.

LibraryStatus.description: Where this workspace's library stands on analysis: watched and searchable, still waiting, or given up on. Read from POST /v1/corpus/ask when reason is needs_analysis or analysis_running or when an answer was drawn from part of the library, and from POST /v1/library/analyze.

videos_waiting_for_analysis.description: Could be watched, has not been yet. This is what blocks POST /v1/corpus/ask until it reaches zero, inside the asked window.

videos_that_could_not_be_analyzed.description: Tried and failed, or had nothing to fetch. Reported, never blocking: a video that will never download must not hold every answer hostage.

videos_of_unknown_length.description: A subset of videos_waiting_for_analysis, not an addition to it: nobody has measured these yet. Longer videos are billed per length rather than a single flat price, and an unmeasured video is priced as a short one until it is; the actual charge never goes above the amount held when the analysis starts.

estimated_cost_usd.description: What analyzing the waiting videos is estimated to cost, priced per step each one still needs, and by length past 3 minutes. On `POST /v1/library/analyze` it is the estimate for this pass only. Absent on a `/v1/corpus/ask` answer while a pass is already running.

analysis_in_progress.description: The run already catching this library up, when one is running. Check it with GET /v1/collections/{collection_id}.

estimated_cost_usd.description: With `field`: what analyzing the first waiting video is estimated to cost. With `held_usd`: what this pass is estimated to cost. Nothing was started or charged.

field.description: Present when max_cost_usd itself was below the estimate.

held_usd.description: Present when the workspace's own call cap, not max_cost_usd, is what fell short of the estimate.

reset_at.description: Unix ms when this key's request window resets.

message.description: Carries the provider's own error text, verbatim.

PilotEvidence.description: Curated identity evidence imported for a pilot workspace, reported separately from the video's own analysis. Null on every row that carries none, which is nearly every row. `caption_mention` is not proof a product is depicted, and `reviewed_family` is provisional AI review, not human or catalog verification. Rows whose status is `unknown`, `rejected` or `conflicted` are not eligible and are withheld from evidence.

policyVersion.description: The eligibility policy the importer applied.

snapshotDate.description: Date of the source archive snapshot. Metrics were not independently rechecked at that time.

targetContext.description: `parent_post_only`: the evidence is about the parent post, not the row it is attached to.

OnScreen.description: What the video SHOWS, recorded once when it was analyzed, separately from what is said. The facets are closed vocabularies so many videos can be counted against each other; the free text is short and timed so it can be quoted. Null for a video analyzed before this record existed, which is not the same as a video that shows nothing.

mood.description: The tone the visuals and delivery convey.

actions.description: What people are visibly doing, as short verb phrases.

productsShown.description: Products the video features, or whose brand is legible on screen.

brand.description: As it appears on the product or packaging. Empty string when none is legible.

startTime.description: Seconds from the start when it first appears.

onScreenText.description: Titles, overlays, prices, labels and signs, copied exactly.

scenes.description: The timed visual log, in order.

AcrossVideos.description: Deterministic counts over the cited videos' stored sentiment and on-screen records, so a comparison is built on numbers rather than tallied by eye from the paragraphs. No model judgment. Present only when at least two videos were cited. Each list is sorted by count and holds at most 8 rows.

with_on_screen.description: How many of them have an on-screen record. The on-screen counts below are out of this number, never out of `videos`.

videos.description: Videos with this value. Each video counts once per value.

sentiment.description: The creator's overall valence, from each video's stored analysis.

brands_shown.description: Brands legible on screen, counted per video. Spellings that differ only in case, spaces or punctuation count as one brand.

videos.description: Videos with this value. Each video counts once per value.

products.description: Product types counted per video, from a product-type mapping when one was made, otherwise from folded exact product names.

videos.description: Videos with this value. Each video counts once per value.

recurring_actions.description: Visible actions that recur in more than one video.

RecordRow.description: One row of the library as stored. Fields the platform never supplied are omitted rather than zero.

views.description: Observed content views, never ad impressions.

skus.description: Brand-profile products whose name appears in the caption.

sentiment.description: The video's overall valence from its stored analysis. Null when the video has not been analyzed.

judgeExcluded.description: True when the subject check (or pilot evidence) excluded the row. Only ever true when `include_excluded=true` let it through.

sample.description: Every post the provider returned, in page order. Nothing is saved.

views.description: Observed content views, never ad impressions.

mention_subject.description: Share of those posts, 0 to 1, whose caption names the subject. 0 when the page was empty.

mention_rate.description: Share of all returned posts, 0 to 1, whose caption names the subject.

suggestion.description: A sentence to show a person: what to try when the subject is matching something else.

label.description: What the step does, in words a person reads.

tool.description: The MCP tool that performs it. Each maps to an endpoint here: `ask_library` is `POST /v1/corpus/ask`, `get_video` is `GET /v1/videos/{video_id}`, `library_overview` is `GET /v1/library`, `analyze_library` is `POST /v1/library/analyze`, `get_collection` is `GET /v1/collections/{collection_id}`.

ActionSet.description: What the result offers next. A step that is not wired is listed under `unavailable` with its reason, never silently left out.

videos.description: Videos that count: analyzed, waiting and could not be analyzed.

waiting_for_analysis.description: Not analyzed yet. An ask answers without them, and says so, until they are; when nothing at all is analyzed it returns `needs_analysis`.

text_posts.description: Reddit and other text posts: in the library, never analyzed as video.

duplicates_folded.description: Copies folded into their duplicate cluster's representative.

most_videos.description: Creators with the most videos in this library. A count of what was collected, not of what they post or how they perform.

subjects.description: Recent collections' subjects, newest first. Library analysis passes and imports are left out.

post_id.description: The video's id in this library.

answer.description: One paragraph per answering video, each with its citation, as on `POST /v1/corpus/ask`.

videos_answering.description: Videos the addressing judge said address the question. Only these are counted, leaned and quoted.

videos_unjudged.description: Videos kept whose addressing could not be judged (the judge timed out or failed). They are not counted in `lean` and not quoted.

indexes_unavailable.description: Indexes that could not be searched. Non-null means a partial result, and `caveat` says so.

degraded.description: Present when some reads fell back (provider limits, timeouts, shared capacity).

lean.description: How the answering videos lean on this question's own subject, judged from each video's answer, not its overall mood.

leans.description: Null under 5 placed videos. `mostly` needs 60% of them on one side; otherwise `divided`.

says.description: What this video's own answer says about the question. Only lines in quotation marks are verbatim transcript; the rest is the model's reading of the video.

across_videos.description: As on `POST /v1/corpus/ask`, over the answering videos.

paid_withheld.description: Videos left out of this question as ads or sponsored. Present only when some were.

others_share.description: Percent of that side's videos with a known value.

difference_points.description: Percentage points; positive means more common among outperformers.

videos_read.description: Videos read after the window, platform and term filters. Billed as `content_enriched`.

too_recent.description: Under 3 days old: views still climbing.

no_creator.description: No creator handle, so no creator median to measure against.

no_posted_date.description: No posting date, so its age cannot be checked.

creator_has_too_few_videos.description: From creators with fewer than 3 videos here, so no median to measure against.

comparison.description: Per attribute (format, setting, people_on_screen, creator_on_camera, mood, length, platform), each value's share among outperformers against the other comparable videos, most over-represented first. min_rise_ratio.description: A trait also rises when its recent share is at least this many times the share in the days before, with `min_relative_videos` recent videos and a gain of `min_relative_points`.

min_relative_videos.description: Recent videos a trait needs before the relative rise applies.

min_relative_points.description: Points a trait's recent share must gain on the days before under the relative rise.

rising.description: Rising and new traits, strongest change first, at most 8. Empty when `rising_withheld_because` is set.

biggest_this_week.description: Traits by video count in the recent period, over the floor only.

traits.description: Every trait that reached the floor in either period, by change, at most 60.

status.description: `new`: rising with no video in the prior period. `not_comparable`: too few videos recorded the field in one period to compare.

example_ids.description: Up to 4 of the trait's recent videos, most viewed first.

formats.description: On-screen formats of the trait's recent videos. Empty for a format trait.

topics.description: The named topics requested, every one, a zero included, ordered as requested. Named topics also appear among `rising`, `traits` and `cards` (where they lead) when they qualify.

rows.description: Rising and new traits, strongest change first, at most 8. Empty when `rising_withheld_because` is set.

below_floor.description: Traits seen in the recent period but under the floor: counted, never ranked.

withheld.description: Rows never counted: own_posts, official_accounts, off_subject (judge-dropped), excluded_topics, other_platforms, text_posts (Reddit).

status.description: `new`: rising with no video in the prior period. `not_comparable`: too few videos recorded the field in one period to compare.

share_recent.description: Percent of the recent period's videos that recorded this kind of field. Null when none did.

change_points.description: share_recent minus share_window, in percentage points. Null when the kind is not comparable.

median_views.description: Median observed views of the trait's videos in the window.

median_engagement_pct.description: Median of (likes + comments + shares) / views, per video, as a percentage.

evidence_ids.description: Ids of listed videos with this trait, recent first, most viewed first, at most 24. Only videos in `evidence` are listed; the counts include the rest.

CollectionPlanSearch.description: One search in a collection plan: a keyword, a hashtag or a creator's account. Run, it becomes one collection.

subject.description: The search, trimmed: words, a tag without `#`, or a handle without `@`.

label.description: How the search reads to people: `"north face"`, `#northface` or `@thenorthface`.

target.description: This search's share of the plan's total target.

reason.description: Why this search serves the goal.

preview.description: What one page of this search returned when it was last checked. Null until it is checked, or when its check failed (not charged).

mention_rate.description: Share of the returned posts on subject: whose caption names it, or for a creator search, that the account itself posted.

returned.description: Posts the preview page returned, across platforms.

suggestion.description: How to revise the search. Null when the verdict is `looks_right`.

collection_id.description: The collection this search became, once the plan is started. Null before that.

checked_at.description: Unix ms of its last check; null when it has none.

CollectionPlan.description: A collection plan: the searches for one brief, proposed for free, checked and quoted together, then run with one `POST /v1/collections` carrying `plan_id`, one collection per search.

goal.description: What the research is for, in the user's words. Null on plans made before goals were asked for.

status.description: `proposed`: free and editable, never checked. `draft`: checked and quoted, can be run until `expires_at`. `started` once its collections exist. `expired`: past `expires_at`; edit it to make it a proposal again, or check it again.

window_hours.description: How far back every search collects.

posted_from.description: First day of the fixed range of posting dates every search keeps; it wins over window_hours, YYYY-MM-DD in UTC. Null for a window that ends now.

posted_to.description: Last day of the range, inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD in UTC. Null for a window that ends now.

target.description: Total videos for the plan, the sum of the searches' targets.

include_paid.description: Whether ads and sponsored videos may be chosen for analysis. When false they are kept in the library, unanalyzed and uncharged.

estimate.description: The sum of each search's `/v1/collections` estimate. Run the plan with `budget_usd` at least `cost_usd.expected`.

eta_minutes.description: The searches run side by side, so this is the slowest one's estimate.

expires_at.description: Unix ms. A proposal is kept for 7 days. A checked plan can be run until its oldest check is 24 hours old, because checks and the quote describe that day's search results.

started_at.description: Unix ms, or null until the plan is run.

confirm_before_running.description: Searches the user must agree to by name before the plan runs: any whose check was `mixed` or `looks_wrong`, returned nothing, failed, or has not been checked. A keyword search is named by its subject, a hashtag as `#tag` and a creator as `@handle`; pass them in `confirm_searches` when the plan is run. Ask about each: revise or drop it (edit the plan and check again), or keep it.

coverage.description: Whether the searches are broad enough for the plan's target. A search returns its strongest matches first, so more videos call for more searches and more kinds of search.

recommended_searches.description: How many searches a plan of this target is well served by.

notes.description: What the searches leave out for this size, one sentence each.

suggested_searches.description: Searches worth adding, each with why. A starting point for the conversation, not a decision.
